## Context
Entity extraction in Biblicus does not use a language model today (spaCy NER, dependency relations, co-occurrence). New fast extraction models built on cheaper decision models may do typed entity and relation extraction at lower cost and higher quality than spaCy labels. Evaluate them against the current pipeline for the needs of a publication knowledge base: typed kinds (maker, task, technique, licence) and typed relations (made_by, built_on, replaces).

This is an exploration. Its output is a written recommendation, not a production extractor. It informs the typed-entity extractor story under the same epic (blbs-d380cb). Papyrus consumer: PPY-428252.

Rule: apply the same protocol to every candidate, with no extra help for any baseline (benchmark parity). Any language-model baseline defaults to the cheap GPT-6 Luna tier unless stated otherwise; any other provider or model needs explicit approval before a run.

## Acceptance criteria
\`\`\`gherkin
Feature: Extractor evaluation
  Scenario: Labelled evaluation set
    Given a labelled set of at least 100 short documents with typed entities and relations
    And a closed vocabulary file
    When every candidate extractor runs under the same protocol
    Then precision, recall and F1 are reported per entity kind and per relation type

  Scenario: Speed and cost
    Then the report includes median and p95 latency per document and cost per 1,000 documents for each candidate

  Scenario: Recommendation
    Then the report recommends a backend for the typed-entity extractor
    And states the failure modes seen, including hallucinated entities and unresolved aliases
\`\`\`

## Candidates
Current spaCy pipeline (baseline), decision-model-based extractors, and a cheap language-model baseline. Record the version and configuration of each.
